newsitem.title: USA: CompDent hits year-low on revenues fears.
newsitem.headline: CompDent hits year-low on revenues fears.

text.p: Shares of CompDent Corp dropped nearly 30 percent amid fears that its revenue growth will not meet historic levels, analysts said.
CompDent slide six points to 14-1/2, a 52-week low.
"Some people are getting indications that top-line revenue growth is not going to be what people expect," said Pamela Menefee, an analyst with Robinson-Humphrey.

CompDent typically posts top-line revenue growth close to the mid-teens. Although the CompDent should see some growth over its fourth quarter revenues of $37.7 million, Wall Street fears the growth may be less normal, Menefee said.
CompDent, which is expected to report first quarter earnings on Tuesday, could not be reached for comment.
On a consensus basis, analysts expect CompDent to earn $0.28 a share, compared with $0.22 a share last year, according to First Call.

Ken Laudan, an analyst with Hambrecht & Quist, said he expects CompDent's quarterly results to be on-target, but said results for the second half of the year may be weak due to a slowdown in acquisitions.

Valuations of publicly-traded companies have weakened amid weakness in the stock market this year. These lower valuations limit companies' ability to acquire private companies in exchange for their stock, Laudan said.
For companies such as CompDent, "the ability to do acquisitions will be hurt. There are probably some deals that won't get done this year," Laudan said.
CompDent provides a full product line of dental care plans, including managed dental care, referral fee-for-service and third party administration.
